units.title: Continuous paths give vanishing transport cost
units.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). For every fixed \(s\in T\), the Kantorovich cost with cost \(c\) from \(\mu_t\) to \(\mu_s\) tends to zero as \(t\to s\). The limit is in the extended nonnegative reals.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.
units.boundary: The cost need not be a metric or symmetric. Compactness and the finite continuous cost are retained. This is a limit at each fixed time, without a quantitative rate.

proof.title: Use the same sample at two times
proof.text: The joint law of \((X_t,X_s)\) has marginals \(\mu_t,\mu_s\). Its paths vary continuously with \(t\), so the existing marginal-law theorem gives weak continuity of this joint law.

proof.title: Integrate the continuous cost
proof.text: On the compact product, integration of the finite continuous nonnegative cost is continuous in the probability law. At \(s\), both coordinates coincide, so this cost integral is zero.

proof.title: Bound the infimum by this coupling
proof.text: The transport cost is nonnegative and at most the cost of the explicit coupling. Squeezing gives the asserted limit.

units.title: A transport estimate gives joint continuity
units.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). Let \(F\) be a normed additive commutative group, \(U:T\times E\to F\) any field, and \(L\in\mathbb R\). Suppose the bound below holds for every pair \((t,x),(s,y)\). Then \(U\) is jointly continuous. Here \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) denotes the probability couplings, and \(\operatorname{toReal}\) is the real-value map on the extended nonnegative reals.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.
\(F\) is a normed additive commutative group; no scalar action or completeness is required.
The displayed estimate holds for all pairs in \(T\times E\), with one real constant \(L\). No sign assumption on \(L\), or prior regularity of \(U\), is required.
units.boundary: The estimate is an explicit input to this general continuity principle. A model application must establish it separately. The proof uses continuity of the extended-real toReal map at zero; no separate finite-cost premise is inserted.

proof.title: Apply the transport limit to the squared cost
proof.text: Fix \(q=(s,y)\). The squared cost is continuous, nonnegative and zero on the diagonal. The preceding theorem, composed with the time projection, gives the transport limit.

proof.title: Make the majorant tend to zero
proof.text: The real-value map is continuous at the finite value zero, and square root is continuous. The point cost tends to its diagonal value. Adding these terms and multiplying by the fixed real constant gives a vanishing majorant.

proof.title: Squeeze the norm difference
proof.text: The assumed estimate bounds the nonnegative norm by that majorant. The norm difference tends to zero at every \(q\), which is joint continuity.
